title: When the Wolf Falls
premise: August Ravensworth has spent a lifetime charting the Thornfell mountains for smugglers, keeping their own past buried with the family they lost to the last dragon war. When a dying courier presses them a living map — one that shifts, breathes, and burns its way into August's skin — they discover it is the key to the Emberhold, where the final dragon, Vessarion, sleeps on the last coals of her kind. Hunted by the Ashen Order, who want the map to kill Vessarion and seize dragon-fire as a weapon, August gathers an unlikely found family: a disgraced order-defector, a fire-singer child, and a smuggler who once betrayed them. At the Emberhold, August learns the truth: their bloodline made the map, and only a Ravensworth can choose whether the last dragon wakes or dies. August chooses to wake her — not as a weapon but as a witness — shattering the Order's claim to power and igniting a fragile new age in which maps are drawn for wonder instead of conquest.
about_author: Ansel Underhill is the pen name of a former trail guide who swears half the passes in this book are real and refuses to say which ones. They write fantasy about people who carry too much and trust too little, usually near mountains.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: August Ravensworth, POV. In the smuggling town of Greymoss, August sells routes through the Thornfells and dodges questions about their past. A stranger arrives bleeding, mutters 'the map chose wrong,' and dies pressing a folded scrap of shifting parchment into August's hands. Emotional beat: wary isolation cracked open by obligation.

chapters.title: Ink That Breathes
chapters.summary: August, POV. The map won't stay folded; it redraws itself nightly, showing paths that don't exist yet, and burns August's palm when they try to sell it. An Ashen Order hunter arrives asking after a courier. August flees Greymoss with nothing but the map and old guilt. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Hospitality
chapters.summary: August, POV, with interludes from Sera Vane, the defected Order archivist tracking them. August seeks help from Wren Calloway, the smuggler who sold them out years ago. Wren agrees to guide them — for the map's secret. Uneasy alliance forms over a shared enemy. Beat: bitter reconciliation beginning.

chapters.title: The Child Who Sang to Coals
chapters.summary: Sera Vane, POV. Sera abandons the Order after witnessing them burn a village hunting a 'fire-touched' child, Pip, who can coax flame from ash. Sera defects and intercepts August's party, bringing Pip and proof the Order means to weaponize dragon-fire. Beat: compassion overriding duty; the found family takes shape.

chapters.title: What the Mountains Remember
chapters.summary: August, POV. The party crosses the Weeping Stair, where the map reveals ruins of the old dragon courts — and August recognizes the sigil of House Ravensworth carved above the gate. Their ancestors were the dragons' mapmakers, oath-bound keepers. Beat: identity upended; grief for a hidden inheritance.

chapters.title: The Order Closes Its Fist
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Ambushed at Thornfell Pass, the group is saved when Wren burns his old smuggling network's loyalty to buy their escape — and is wounded. Pip's fire flares uncontrollably; Sera realizes the Order has been breeding fire-singers as living fuses. Beat: sacrifice, and stakes made brutally personal.

chapters.title: Emberhold
chapters.summary: August, POV. Following the map's final line, they reach the Emberhold: a caldera fortress where Vessarion sleeps coiled around the last dragon-fire. The map dissolves into August's skin, revealing the choice written into their blood — wake her or let her gutter out. The Order arrives at the rim. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Price of the Pen
chapters.summary: Sera, POV. The Order's commander offers August absolution: die willingly, and your blood opens the vault without a fight. Wren and Pip are taken hostage. Sera turns the Order's own archives against them, exposing the commander's plan to enslave Vessarion's fire. Beat: courage in the face of impossible bargains.

chapters.title: When the Wolf Falls
chapters.summary: August, POV. Climax. August walks into the Emberhold as the Order breaches it, choosing neither martyrdom nor murder: they speak the old cartographer's oath and wake Vessarion as a witness, not a weapon. Dragon-fire judges the commander's ambition; Wren breaks the hostages free; the Order fractures. Beat: self-acceptance — August stops running from what they are.

chapters.title: Blank Spaces
chapters.summary: August, POV, epilogue-like. Months later, August draws new maps — some blank on purpose, left for travelers to fill. Vessarion roosts above Greymoss as guardian rather than god; Pip studies under Sera; Wren rebuilds honest roads. August signs one map 'for whoever comes next.' Beat: quiet hope; a family, and a world, still being drawn.
